title: General Aiptasia Husbandry Protocol
author: OSU Weis Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rihd4b6

steps.title: Set light conditions
steps.instruction: Provide white light (≥10 000 K) for symbiotic Aiptasia at 10–40 µmol photons mm⁻² s⁻¹; keep aposymbiotic Aiptasia in complete darkness (0 µmol photons mm⁻² s⁻¹) by storing them in dark containers, only exposing them to light for feeding or cleaning. Any LED strip, fluorescent tube, or other bulb type is acceptable as long as the white light intensity meets the specified range.

steps.title: Prepare artificial seawater (ASW)
steps.instruction: Mix artificial seawater using RO/DI water (avoid tap water) and Instant Ocean salt mix according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Adjust to a salinity of ~33 ppt (as read on a refractometer) and pH 8.0. Use a 32‑gallon (~121 L) Brute trash‑can container equipped with a submersible pump at the bottom to circulate the water. Once the target salinity is reached, pump the ASW into 5‑gallon (~19 L) carboys for storage and use in the lab.

steps.title: Maintain stock temperature
steps.instruction: Keep general stock cultures at 20–26 °C, ideally 25 °C. Cultures used for spawning should be maintained at 29 °C.

steps.title: Set up storage containers
steps.instruction: For backup or large numbers of anemones use small aquaria of 2.5–10 gallons with good water flow provided by a powerhead or a large airstone; a filter is recommended to keep water clear and reduce cleaning frequency. Low‑number clonal lines or experimental groups can be kept in Cambro plastic food storage containers (including black containers for aposymbiotic anemones). Do not overcrowd the containers.

steps.title: Prepare brine shrimp culture
steps.instruction: Order premium brine shrimp eggs (e.g., from Brine Shrimp Direct). Hatch a batch on Monday to be harvested on Wednesday, a batch on Wednesday to be harvested on Friday, and a batch on Friday to be harvested on the following Monday (or Saturday if needed).

steps.title: Feed Aiptasia
steps.instruction: Feed anemones at least three times per week using harvested brine shrimp. Saturate the container with shrimp to maximize intake, but remove any uneaten food promptly to prevent water fouling. Increasing the number of feeding days per week should increase anemone growth rate.

steps.title: Clean containers after feeding
steps.instruction: Wait at least 1 hour after feeding (preferably >3 hours, but no longer than 8 hours) before cleaning. Dump the water, taking care not to lose detached anemones. Use cotton swabs to remove algae from container surfaces while avoiding disturbance of anemones or pedal lacerates. If algae are extensive, move anemones to a fresh container and proceed to bleach the old container (see Bleach step).

steps.title: Weekly water‑change schedule
steps.instruction: Follow the daily routine below to keep water quality high and ensure a continuous supply of fresh ASW.

substeps.instruction: Monday morning: Feed Aiptasia with brine shrimp; start a new brine‑shrimp batch for Wednesday harvest; spot‑check all containers for unhealthy or dying anemones; test salinity in backup stock aquaria and adjust to ~33 ppt if needed.

Monday afternoon: Clean all Aiptasia containers and replace water with newly prepared ASW; start a new batch of ASW in the 32‑gallon container. If containers develop hard‑to‑swab algae, transfer anemones to fresh containers and begin bleaching the old containers.
Tuesday: Distribute ASW from the 32‑gallon batch into 5‑gallon carboys for storage; start another fresh batch of ASW in the 32‑gallon container.
Wednesday morning: Feed Aiptasia; start a new brine‑shrimp batch for Friday harvest; spot‑check containers; if Tuesday’s ASW distribution was missed, distribute ASW to carboys and start a new batch.
Wednesday afternoon: Clean all Aiptasia containers and replace water with fresh ASW.
Thursday: Distribute ASW to carboys and start a new batch; rinse and wipe down the 32‑gallon container with DI water.

Friday morning: Feed Aiptasia; start a new brine‑shrimp batch for Monday (or Saturday) harvest; spot‑check containers; if Thursday’s ASW distribution was missed, distribute ASW to carboys and start a new batch; rinse and wipe down the 32‑gallon container with DI water.
Friday afternoon: Clean all Aiptasia containers and replace water with fresh ASW.

steps.title: Bleach containers when needed
steps.instruction: Soak containers (and optionally ASW carboys) in a ~10 % sodium‑hypochlorite (bleach) solution overnight to remove encrusted algae. Scrub the surfaces to dislodge remaining algae. Rinse thoroughly with DI water over 2–3 days, replacing the rinse water each day. Add a water conditioner to the final rinse to neutralize any residual chlorine or chloramine ions.

steps.title: Monitor health and adjust salinity
steps.instruction: Perform daily spot checks for unhealthy or dying anemones. Test salinity in backup stock aquaria each morning and adjust to ~33 ppt as needed. Recognize common causes of mortality: hypoxia, incorrect salinity, improper temperature, bleach contamination, or microbial buildup from waste food or decaying anemones.
